x: Allan Dunn has been called up to H.M.S.
In the field events we had hopes that Alan Dunn would at least be able to reproduce or perhaps improve on his last year's performances and so gain a place in the Javelin.

Alan Dunn, of whom great things were expected this season, did not quite reach the heights expected in the Junior events, but did a wonderful throw of over 160 feet with a senior Javelin in the first of the A.A.A. handicaps, to win.

He is at Catterick with the Royal Signals, and hopes to compete in the Army Track Championships this year. Allan Dunn is with Combined Operations at Troon, and hopes to have a few runs on the beach to keep fit.

Our Javelin throwers, Charlie Melchior, Alan Dunn and veteran George Powell have not shown performances up to their best, but Charlie again won the Hertfordshire County Championship and the Club Championship with a throw of 154 feet 3 inches.

However, it is to Alan Dunn, Geoff Jarvis, Arthur Allen and Terry Bateman we look for improved performances and from at least one, distances approaching, even if not beating those achieved by the old stalwarts in previous years.
If Alan Dunn is now fully recovered from his arm injury he should be our first string backed up by Bateman, Higgins and Bergvalds. Arthur Allen it is hoped will show 150 to 160 feet in this event.
